clause: It renders as a FACT, not an affordance: no href/mailto, because a named person's home address dressed as a tappable control overstates what it is.
reason: The load-bearing obligation — a candidate's filed address is public information and renders — is conserved by R-0256 ('A candidate's filed mailing address renders — it is public information. A contact that reaches an office rather than a person is published, labelled as the office'). The 'no href/mailto, render as a fact not an affordance' instruction is presentation-level rendering detail (a 'how'), a code-level styling choice, not a distinct constitutional bar/prohibition/proof-standard.

clause: Bodies that CERTAINLY govern render normally with no marker; a body that MAY OR MAY NOT govern renders with a per-body pill 'Could govern you — add your address to confirm.'
reason: Superseded UI mechanism. R-0256 replaced the per-body ambiguity pill with a cleaner scope model that carries the same obligation: 'Before a confirmed address the scope is the ZIP: every governing entity intersecting it renders. After a confirmed address the scope is the address: only entities that govern it render.' The non-assertion of governance pre-address, and the address-narrowing invitation, are conserved by that model; the specific pill is a retired presentation mechanism, not a surviving distinct obligation.

clause: The pill is an invitation, not a disclosure of our incompleteness; RULING 44 (per-card completeness) is NOT weakened by it.
reason: Rides entirely on the retired per-body pill mechanism (see prior item). The surviving underlying obligation — per-card/per-field completeness is not weakened by another field's state — is conserved by R-0254 ('A gap in one field has no bearing on any other field, candidate or contest'). Pure elaboration of a preserved obligation tied to a superseded mechanism.

clause: A ZCTA centroid may never resolve a ballot or a who-governs answer.
quote: A ZIP cannot answer "who governs you"; a street address can.

clause: It does not widen to claim every municipality in the zip governs the reader; the card's verb is GOVERN.
quote: Before a confirmed address the scope is the ZIP: every governing entity intersecting it renders.

clause: It supplies no prose beyond the labelled self-description the blurb rule governs, and it NEVER supplies a photo.
quote: A photo ships through one of four doors — explicit licence, official government portrait, campaign self-published portrait, last-resort .gov or campaign site — and only an author-reviewed image renders

clause: The verification bar does not move: the presence must be the candidate's OWN, established by name–office–cycle agreement and control-checked; a page found by guessing a handle is a LEAD, never a HIT.
quote: a guessed identifier yields a `LEAD`, never a `HIT`

clause: It NEVER supplies a photo — social-media images are prohibited at every door of the photo rule, and a door the campaign-site rule opens is not a door into the photo rule.
restoreText: Social-media images are never a portrait source at any of the four photo doors — a candidate's self-published social image does not become a usable portrait, and a compliant route that fills the campaign-site field is not thereby a photo door.
reason: Whole-corpus check confirms the specific prohibition is carried nowhere. R-0255's four doors include 'campaign self-published portrait' and 'last-resort .gov or campaign site'; a candidate's own social-media profile photo reads as campaign-self-published and could render (author-reviewed) under R-0255 — exactly what R-0145 forbids at EVERY door. R-0255 makes no social-media carve-out, so the distinct bar (the highest-risk clause the predecessor itself flagged) is lost.

clause: It supplies no prose beyond the labelled self-description the blurb rule already governs.
quote: LLM summaries paraphrase a cited source and never fill a gap. Every blurb carries its source class.

clause: The ZIP-scoped view is one tap away: clearing the address restores it in full.
reason: Operational UX affordance (a 'how'). The scope model it depends on is conserved by R-0256 ('Once given, an address persists for the session and resolves every surface that could use it'); one-tap reversibility of the address is a presentation-level affordance, not a distinct constitutional obligation/bar.

clause: A row at an overlapping level (school district, municipality) has been determined NOTHING about and stays exactly as it was; dropping it would be the manufactured claim CLAUDE.md forbids, in the other direction.
restoreText: After an address narrows scope, an overlapping body whose governance of the reader has been determined to be nothing — neither confirmed nor excluded — stays exactly as it was; dropping it manufactures a false claim that it does not govern the reader.
reason: R-0256's post-address rule 'only entities that govern it render' is binary and does not address the undetermined case; a literal reading drops an overlapping body nothing has been established about. Nothing in the corpus preserves the safeguard that an undetermined overlapping row must remain, and R-0256's 'not yours label is prohibited' governs annotation, not dropping. The transparency mandate's 'absence is never asserted' speaks to record acquisition, not to manufacturing a negative governance claim by omission. Distinct safeguard carried nowhere.

clause: A change is kept ONLY IF the rebuilt number actually FELL.
reason: Operational acceptance detail elaborating R-0257's measurement requirement ('A performance change ships with its before-and-after measurement; an instrument without a committed baseline is unfinished'). The measurement exists precisely to decide whether to keep the change; 'kept only if the number fell' is the process-level consequence of that preserved obligation, not a distinct constitutional bar. Low reader-truth stakes (internal performance).

clause: A speed change that alters an answer is a wrong answer that arrived faster.
quote: Reader-facing behaviour is never degraded to fix an internal problem.

clause: A dishonest baseline is worse than none; a run that cannot produce a true baseline is not committed — the row stays open with the measurement attached rather than closing on a bad number.
quote: an instrument without a committed baseline is unfinished.

clause: A verification that cannot reach the reader's route says so, and the item is a BOUNDARY STOP rather than a finish.
quote: A check that cannot run says so.

clause: A calendar date is read from the string and never round-tripped through a Date; a UTC midnight formatted in a local zone yields an off-by-one date, which in this product is a false claim about a government.
reason: Operational/code-level correctness technique. The governing principle — a wrong date is a false claim about a government and correctness is paramount — is conserved by R-0273 ('A fast wrong answer is a false claim about a government ... never trade an honest gap for a plausible guess') and the transparency mandate. The centralizing mechanism is conserved by R-0258's single date formatter ('Dates spell out ... through one formatter, product-wide'), which is where the no-round-trip handling is enforced. The specific 'do not round-trip through a Date' instruction is implementation detail, not a distinct constitutional bar.

clause: Flagged text is preserved with full metadata, never silently deleted (deletion destroys evidence).
quote: Severe content goes to a HELD queue for the author's review under `docs/abuse-policy.md`.

clause: Flagging never auto-reports; every report passes human review first.
quote: Nothing is auto-forwarded. Severe content goes to a HELD queue for the author's review

clause: 'May', never 'will.' — the sharing disclosure is a stated commitment, not a guarantee that it will be shared.
quote: threats of violence are removed and *may* be reported. "May," never "will."

clause: 'MAY', never 'will' — the fine print carries the may-not-will commitment (a stated commitment not honored every instance is worse than a reserved right).
The THREAT NOTICE does not move — it remains required adjacent to any free-text field about named real people (Speak Your Mind is such a field).
quote: Every free-text field about named real people carries a threat notice
